newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hoechst-HMR unit posts Q1 16.5 pct profit margin.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst-HMR unit posts Q1 16.5 pct profit margin.

text.p: German chemicals and drugs group Hoechst AG said on Monday that its Hoechst Marion Roussel drugs unit posted a 16.5 percent operating margin in the first quarter of 1997.

"In the first quarter of 1997 the operating margin was 16.5 percent as compared with an operating margin of 15.7 percent in the first quarter of 1996," Daniel Camus, chief financial officer at HMR told a conference call.
The group also said that last year's underlying profit margin was at 14.3 percent for the full year.

Camus added however that the group still planned to reach its 20 percent operating margin goal by 1999, one year later than initially planned due to goodwill related to the purchase of an outstanding stake in Roussel Uclaf RUCF.PA.
"The target of 20 percent remains," Camus said.
The group also said that its newly launched allergy drug Allegra had performed very well in the U.S. "It is a beautiful cash contributor to HMR," Camus said.
Allegra has helped offset problems created when the U.S. Food and Drug Administration proposed banning another Hoechst product, antihistimine Seldane.
